FieldShift – Climate-Smart Crop Rotation Planner

FieldShift is a climate-smart agriculture prototype developed for Chakwal District, Pakistan. It uses NASA POWER climate data from 2015 to 2025 to explore temperature and rainfall patterns and their potential impact on agricultural planning.

We developed an interactive web dashboard featuring a map of Chakwal District, climate data visualizations, annual temperature and rainfall summaries, and exploratory crop rotation options such as Wheat–Chickpea, Millet–Groundnut, and Wheat–Pulse.

FieldShift addresses the challenge of climate uncertainty in agriculture by making climate information easier to understand and connecting it with potential crop rotation strategies. It demonstrates how NASA Earth observation data and geospatial technology can support more informed agricultural decisions.

This project is important because changing weather and rainfall variability create challenges for farmers. FieldShift provides a starting point for climate-aware farming and future agricultural research. Its crop rotation options are exploratory and require further validation using local soil data and agricultural expertise.
details:
FieldShift – Climate-Smart Crop Rotation Planner

FieldShift is an interactive climate-smart agriculture prototype developed for Chakwal District, Pakistan. It aims to demonstrate how NASA Earth observation data can help explore climate patterns and support better agricultural planning.

How Does It Work?

FieldShift uses NASA POWER daily climate data from 2015 to 2025, including temperature and precipitation observations. We processed the data using Python to calculate annual climate summaries. The web dashboard displays an interactive map of Chakwal District, annual temperature and rainfall charts, and possible crop rotation options such as Wheat–Chickpea, Millet–Groundnut, and Wheat–Pulse.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project makes climate information easier to understand through maps and visualizations. It provides a starting point for exploring climate-aware crop rotation and encourages the use of scientific data in agricultural planning. Its long-term goal is to support climate resilience and more informed farming decisions in areas affected by changing weather and rainfall patterns.

Tools and Technologies

  • NASA POWER API: Climate data collection.
  • Python: Data downloading, processing, and analysis.
  • HTML, CSS, and JavaScript: Dashboard development.
  • Leaflet and OpenStreetMap: Interactive mapping.
  • Chart.js: Climate data visualization.
  • QGIS: Geospatial data preparation and district boundary processing.
  • GeoJSON and CSV: Data storage and integration.
  • GitHub: Project version control and sharing.

Creativity and Innovation

FieldShift brings together satellite-based climate observations, geospatial mapping, and crop rotation exploration in one simple dashboard. Instead of presenting raw climate data, it transforms observations into understandable charts and connects them with possible agricultural strategies.

Factors Considered

Our team considered climate variability, temperature patterns, rainfall uncertainty, geographical boundaries, and the importance of crop diversity. We also recognized that soil conditions, water availability, local farming practices, and expert agricultural validation are essential before making actual crop recommendations.

FieldShift is an exploratory prototype, not a validated crop recommendation system. It provides a foundation for future improvements, including soil data integration, crop suitability analysis, and local expert validation.
